topic: Binary-star separation certificates and complete equivalence for singleton-permitting blocked Gaussian DAGs. Revival of parent eid_blocked_colour_reversal_complete: replace its citation-dependent necessity bridge by the precise theorem that every static-signature mismatch is separated by a unit-noise covariance with at most two coefficient-one blocks at one target, integer entries bounded by p, and an exact CI-minor or cleared-regression certificate in {+/-1,+/-2}, yielding B(p)=ceil(log2 p). Prove this constructive certificate theorem together with covariance-model equality iff static-signature equality iff explicitly defined legal singleton covered-reversal connectivity; then give exact component enumeration and the qualified generic fixed-p BIC/simultaneous-effect inference rung. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: exact star formulas and exhaustive rational p<=4 checks separated 1,310,886 differing-signature pairs; a five-node extra-parent/two-reversal witness has cleared difference -1. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: independently prove the all-p four-case router, especially mutual containment in the unequal-family reversed-edge case. EARLY KILL TEST: independently verify the router through p=4, then reproduce p=5 and stress all reversed-family pairs. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/eid_blocked_colour_rational_separation_complete.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Replace the generic-faithfulness necessity bridge by an all-p constructive router assigning every static-signature mismatch a bounded binary-star covariance separator.

source_refs.excerpt: That lemma is supplied without proof or a precise theorem-level citation
This sparse covariance witness is the load-bearing necessity step because it handles arbitrary extra target parents

source_refs.claim: The paper gives rational covariance recovery maps and an ideal-based equivalence test, but no bounded rational witness or bit-complexity theorem for inequivalence.
source_refs.author: Tobias Boege, Kaie Kubjas, Pratik Misra, Liam Solus
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B

source_refs.claim: Trek separation characterizes covariance-submatrix rank constraints through determinant expansions, but does not give bounded witnesses after coefficient-colour equalities are imposed.
source_refs.author: Seth Sullivant, Kelli Talaska, Jan Draisma

source_refs.claim: Restricted trek separation yields exact determinant constraints for graphical models, illustrating certificate machinery without a uniform arithmetic-height guarantee.
source_refs.author: Mathias Drton, Elina Robeva, Luca Weihs

open_problems.why_unsolved: The parent proof first imported an implication from equality of coloured covariance images to ordinary Markov equivalence and then used a sparse reversed-edge regression separator; the cold referee identified the imported implication as an undischarged load-bearing bridge. Published coloured-DAG theory provides generic rational recovery and ideal nonmembership, while trek methods identify determinant vanishing, but neither supplies a uniformly small arithmetic point. A direct proof must route skeleton, collider, target-block-family, and unequal-family orientation mismatches separately. The hard new step is the unequal-family reversed-edge case: both containment directions must be established without assuming the desired collider conclusion, and the chosen one- or two-block star must survive extra parents and simultaneous reversed arrows with a controlled cleared value.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An all-p four-case theorem and algorithm that, for every unequal pair of static signatures, constructs a unit-noise covariance with at most two coefficient-one blocks at one target, integer entries bounded by p, and an exact CI minor or cleared-regression discrepancy in {−2,−1,1,2}, implying B(p)=ceil(log2 p).

writing_exemplar.why: Its progression from coloured covariance geometry to graphical equivalence is the closest framing for replacing abstract model inequality by explicit separating witnesses.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Equal structural coefficients encode causal communities -> singleton colours create nontrivial covariance equivalence -> graphical necessity needs an observable separator -> bounded binary-star certificates distinguish every signature mismatch

method_exemplars.technique: Expand covariance minors as signed trek systems and control cancellation to prove exact rank constraints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired CI certificate is a low-degree determinant whose surviving terms must remain controlled after equal-colour substitutions.

method_exemplars.technique: Convert rational regression restrictions into nested covariance determinants and prove their graphical validity using restricted treks.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The cleared regression discrepancy is a determinant-like polynomial certificate, so restricted-trek arguments are the nearest proof analogue.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate equality-constrained Gaussian structural coefficients by colour-pooled regression and analyze MLE existence and uniqueness through linear-independence conditions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The exact separator identifies a local coefficient-colour mismatch, and pooled restricted regression is the closest sample analogue for exploiting it.

open_problems.open_problem: Give a citation-independent complete equivalence theorem for singleton-permitting blocked Gaussian DAGs in which static-signature equality is exactly legal singleton covered-reversal connectivity.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Boege et al. prove structural identifiability only for proper blocked colourings and explicitly leave the general coloured equivalence problem open; singleton colours permit differently oriented states to share one covariance model. Chickering's theorem controls only ordinary conditional-independence equivalence, and the partial-homoscedastic analogue constrains a different parameter partition. The parent note supplied tangent recovery and legal-reversal sufficiency, but its necessity chain began with the referee-flagged imported Markov-equivalence implication. After direct signature separators are proved, the remaining nontrivial step is to show that every disagreement-decreasing covered reversal selected by Chickering is singleton-block and partition-compatible, and that its partition transport is path-independent.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient theorem equating full covariance-model equality, equality of an explicit skeleton/collider/nonsingleton-family/orientation signature, and connectivity by explicitly defined legal singleton covered reversals, with exact component enumeration and reversal distance equal to arrow disagreement.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames coefficient colours as causal communities and directly motivates graphical and transformational model-equivalence characterizations.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Coefficient colours encode communities of direct causes -> proper non-singleton colour classes identify one DAG -> singleton classes restore observational equivalence -> characterize the class statically and by legal local moves

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the monotone covered-reversal induction that reverses each disagreeing arrow once while preserving ordinary Markov equivalence.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination connectivity graph is a constrained subgraph of Chickering's reversal graph; the changed step is proving singleton and partition-transport legality at each move.

method_exemplars.technique: Recover partition-induced compelled arrows, combine them with a CPDAG, and characterize all consistent DAG extensions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest complete equivalence-class representation for a partition restriction in a linear Gaussian DAG.

method_exemplars.technique: Compute target-local constrained Gaussian likelihoods and decomposable BIC scores, then quotient exact ties by the proved covariance-image components.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the estimation machinery for the coefficient-coloured model whose structural target becomes an equivalence component once singleton blocks are admitted.

open_problems.open_problem: Establish fixed-p generic component-consistent Gaussian BIC selection for singleton-permitting blocked DAGs and simultaneous inference for the component's member-labelled total-effect set.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Smooth-model BIC theory compares a fixed list of model images, whereas singleton blocked-colour states can give several parametrizations of one image and inequivalent components can meet on zero-edge or coincident-colour strata. The first new selection step is to quotient exact likelihood ties and prove that every lower- or equal-dimensional inequivalent image has a positive Gaussian Kullback-Leibler gap at a generic true covariance, with all failures confined to an explicit proper algebraic set. For inference, ordinary IDA limit theory does not cover equality-constrained coefficient models or the full member-labelled effect set after component selection, while test-inversion results show why model-union singularities cannot simply be ignored.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A fixed-p theorem that every global BIC minimizer lies in the true static-signature component with probability tending to one outside an explicit proper algebraic exceptional set, plus a component-indexed estimator and joint delta-method, bootstrap, or test-inversion result giving simultaneous pointwise coverage at least 1−alpha for a fixed finite list of total effects.

writing_exemplar.why: Its GECS section supplies the causal-community motivation, target-local likelihood, decomposable BIC, and explicit consistency gap.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Blocked colours pool causal coefficients -> target-local likelihood makes coloured BIC feasible -> singleton colours change the target from one DAG to an equivalence component -> prove generic component recovery and effect-set uncertainty quantification

method_exemplars.technique: Use smooth curved-exponential-family likelihood expansions to separate misspecified models by order-n loss and overfitted models by the logarithmic dimension penalty.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Blocked Gaussian DAG images are smooth covariance submanifolds; the added step is quotienting equal images and excluding their algebraic intersections generically.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert goodness-of-fit tests over a union of Gaussian SEM strata to cover structural and numerical uncertainty jointly.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A singleton-permitting blocked component is likewise a finite union of constrained Gaussian structural representations with singular intersections.

method_exemplars.technique: Use recursive regressions to estimate simultaneous-intervention effects, derive their asymptotic covariance, and aggregate graph-specific effect vectors over an equivalence class.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired rung needs the same joint effect-functional covariance calculation over a legal blocked-colour component.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct an output-polynomial or polynomial-delay algorithm emitting each distinct rational total-effect functional of a blocked-colour equivalence component exactly once with exact identity and membership certificates.

source_refs.excerpt: The unresolved requirement is deterministic output-sensitive identity and canonicalization
State enumeration can be exponentially more redundant than the causal output

open_problems.why_unsolved: The parent supplies exact-once state enumeration and a canonical partition lift, but different states can induce globally identical rational effect maps. Clearing positive denominators decides identity only after coefficient expansion, which may be exponentially larger than the compact arithmetic circuits and may hide cancellation. The first changed proof step is a canonical compact-circuit identity procedure whose certificate size and delay are charged together with complete identity-class memberships and requested shortest reversal paths; agreement at finitely many covariance matrices cannot certify global identity.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An algorithm and complexity theorem giving output-polynomial total time or polynomial delay for compact representatives of all distinct rational effect maps, exact global-identity certificates, complete state-to-functional membership lists, and optional shortest legal-reversal certificates.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates equivalence-class traversal by the downstream need to report possible causal effects rather than merely list graphs.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Observational data identify a graph class -> class members can imply different total effects -> causal analysis must retain every compatible functional -> blocked components require certified quotienting by global rational identity

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt exact-once linear-delay enumeration of consistent DAG extensions after Meek closure.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Blocked state enumeration already reduces to consistent extensions; the unresolved step is composing that stream with exact rational-functional canonicalization without losing output sensitivity.

method_exemplars.technique: Use clique-picking and minimal-separator recursion to traverse ordinary equivalence classes without duplicate orientations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination similarly needs a canonical recursion, but its output classes are induced rational maps rather than DAGs.

method_exemplars.technique: Attach efficient least-squares estimators and joint covariance calculations to distinct graph-indexed total-effect functionals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies inferential machinery once the exact quotient enumerator has identified the distinct causal functionals.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Ordinary enumeration quotients orientations by skeleton and unshielded colliders, and its local move is any covered reversal. Singleton-permitting blocked models impose a target-family legality condition, so one ordinary Markov-equivalence class can split into several static-signature components with nonuniform sizes. The bounded search found ordinary class counts and fixed-skeleton generating functions but no coloured-component count. The first proof step that changes is the combinatorial state decomposition: it must record nonsingleton target families and orientation constraints and propagate how each covered reversal preserves or changes that state.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An exact recurrence, generating function, or closed formula for the number and cardinality distribution of legal-reversal components for each p and blocked-colour profile, proved through a canonical decomposition of the static-signature reversal graph.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames equivalence-class enumeration as a measure of observational ambiguity and turns graphical invariants into generating functions.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Observational data recover only an equivalence class -> class number and size quantify residual ambiguity -> fixed-skeleton invariants enable exact generating functions -> refine the counting state to blocked-colour signatures

method_exemplars.technique: Represent an equivalence class as the connected graph generated by covered-edge reversals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Blocked components are connected components of a reversal graph obtained by restricting exactly this move set.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive fixed-skeleton generating recurrences by decomposing orientations according to immoralities and class size.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A coloured analogue must replace the immorality-only state by the static signature and propagate legal reversal choices through a similar decomposition.

method_exemplars.technique: Enumerate locally possible parent sets and consistently estimate the resulting set of total causal effects.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Component counts and sizes determine the number of graph-indexed effect functionals that remain after coloured-model selection.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the local asymptotic minimax recovery-or-abstention envelope near blocked-colour model intersections where the binary-star separation signal vanishes.

source_refs.excerpt: no greedy-search consistency or uniform inference near model intersections is asserted
The exact local minimax power envelope at bounded information distance is deliberately open.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Generic fixed-p BIC and effect-set inference exclude algebraic strata where edges vanish, block coefficients coincide, or an orientation separator degenerates. Along contiguous sequences approaching those intersections, the covariance-equivalence component changes discontinuously and regular within-model likelihood expansions do not determine attainable classification probability or honest coverage. The first proof step must derive a local Gaussian experiment for competing tangent cones indexed by the shrinking cleared binary-star certificate, rather than reuse pointwise BIC consistency.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A tangent-cone Gaussian experiment and explicit local minimax correct-component or honest-abstention envelope indexed by the shrinking separator, together with a likelihood-, score-, or certificate-based selector and simultaneous effect-set region attaining that envelope.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames structural uncertainty honestly when one selected causal graph cannot be treated as certain.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Population restrictions distinguish causal structures -> distinguishing signals can shrink at the sampling scale -> generic consistency offers no protection at model intersections -> derive an optimal local recovery or abstention guarantee

method_exemplars.technique: Expand likelihood-ratio information along least-favourable local paths and relate it to the optimal testing-error exponent.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Pairwise component recovery near a vanishing certificate is a local composite testing problem.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert structural goodness-of-fit tests to return honest recovery sets rather than condition inference on one selected graph.
method_exemplars.why_closest: An attaining procedure must remain valid at component intersections where deterministic correct selection is impossible.

literature_map:
Boege, Kubjas, Misra and Solus (JRSSB 2026, arXiv:2404.04024) establish rational Markov properties and smooth geometry for coloured Gaussian DAGs, prove BPEC identifiability only under proper colourings, and pose general edge-colour equivalence as Question 20.
Their Example 5 supplies the key tension: singleton edge colours permit differently oriented and coloured DAGs to define the same covariance model.
Makam, Reichenbach and Seigal (EJS 2023, arXiv:2108.10058) analyze coefficient-equality RDAG models and constrained Gaussian likelihood geometry.
Wu and Drton (IEEE JSAIT 2023, arXiv:2308.08959) solve the parallel equivalence problem for partial equality of innovation variances and construct a generalized CPDAG.
Peters and Buehlmann (Biometrika 2014, DOI 10.1093/biomet/asu076) show how equal error variances identify a linear Gaussian DAG, an adjacent restriction rather than a coefficient-colour result.
Verma and Pearl (UAI 1990) give the ordinary same-skeleton and same-v-structure criterion, and Chickering (UAI 1995) gives its covered-reversal transformation.
Andersson, Madigan and Perlman (Annals of Statistics 1997) encode ordinary equivalence classes by essential graphs with chordal chain components.
Sullivant, Talaska and Draisma (Annals of Statistics 2010) characterize covariance-minor constraints by trek separation.
Drton, Robeva and Weihs (Bernoulli 2020, arXiv:1807.07561) extend exact polynomial constraints through restricted trek separation.
Targeted searches found no bounded unit-noise integer covariance witness or sharp bit-height theorem for inequivalent singleton-permitting blocked Gaussian DAGs.
Gillispie and Perlman (Artificial Intelligence 2002) enumerate ordinary Markov-equivalence classes and their size distributions through ten vertices.
Radhakrishnan, Solus and Uhler (Discrete Applied Mathematics 2018, arXiv:1706.06091) derive fixed-skeleton generating functions and exact tree formulas for ordinary classes, not blocked-colour components.
Wienobst, Luttermann, Bannach and Liskiewicz (AAAI 2023, arXiv:2301.12212) give linear-delay consistent-extension enumeration, but not rational-effect identity quotienting.
Haughton (Annals of Statistics 1988) supplies smooth finite-model BIC asymptotics; Boege et al. leave coloured-search consistency open.
Maathuis, Kalisch and Buehlmann (Annals of Statistics 2009), Nandy, Maathuis and Richardson (Annals of Statistics 2017), and Strieder and Drton (JCI 2023) provide adjacent possible-effect estimation and uncertainty tools, but not simultaneous inference over singleton blocked-colour components.
